title: Domain Name System
source_scope: DNS guide preserved in full. Cross-topic coverage checks are limited to networking lecture guides 01–06; lectures 07 onward are algorithms and were excluded by user instruction.
question_identity: question_id is stable within its source topic; source_index is zero-based in source_quiz. Verify question_sha256 before matching after edits. External questions remain canonical in their own topic manifest.
dependency_convention: required_lesson_ids excludes the primary lesson and lists additional lessons needed for the answer. optional_lesson_ids lists background only. related_lesson_ids is their union. Empty required_lesson_ids means no additional lesson is required for the supported answer concept; wording flags remain independent.

learning_goals: Identify the hostname DNS resolves within a URL.
Explain name resolution as a library service that can consult DNS or local sources.

lessons.title: Why distributed naming and caching scale
learning_goals: Explain why a shared hosts file scales poorly.
Relate read-heavy data and loose consistency to aggressive caching.

lessons.title: Zones, delegation, and recursive resolution
learning_goals: Distinguish a domain from an administrative zone.
Trace stub-to-recursive queries and iterative referrals from root to authority.

lessons.title: Bootstrapping, glue, and delegation inspection
learning_goals: Explain root hints and the circular dependency solved by glue.
Classify nameservers as inside or outside a delegated zone and inspect referrals.

lessons.title: DNS transport and message sections
learning_goals: Explain UDP, TCP framing, EDNS, and truncation fallback.
Identify Question, Answer, Authority, and Additional sections.

lessons.title: DNS headers and resource records
learning_goals: Interpret RD, RA, AA, TC, and the section counts.
Read resource-record fields and distinguish RR TTL from message flags.

lessons.title: Labels, name encoding, and compression
learning_goals: Interpret label lengths and the root terminator.
Decode the 14-bit offset in a two-byte compression pointer.

lessons.title: Replication, SOA, and cache lifetimes
learning_goals: Distinguish secondary refresh from positive and negative caching.
Explain TTL trade-offs and compute a negative lifetime from SOA timing.

lessons.title: CNAME chains and alias restrictions
learning_goals: Follow aliases to provider-managed addresses.
Distinguish indirection from delegation and retain supplementary CNAME/MX restrictions.

lessons.title: Mail exchange and reverse DNS
learning_goals: Use MX priorities to choose mail servers.
Construct reverse names and explain why PTR does not return every alias.

lessons.title: Service discovery, TXT, and SPF
learning_goals: Interpret SRV priority, weight, port, and target.
Explain TXT extensibility and distinguish SPF softfail from neutral.

lessons.title: Round-robin DNS and address selection
learning_goals: Explain how ordered address RRsets distribute client choices.
Distinguish address rotation, health checking, and IP anycast.

lessons.title: Forgery and cache poisoning
learning_goals: Explain how a forged accepted reply can poison a shared cache.
Describe repeated fresh-name attempts and the benefit and limits of source-port randomization.

lessons.title: DNSSEC data authentication and deployment
learning_goals: Trace trust from an anchor through DS, DNSKEY, and RRSIG.
Separate signing, validation, confidentiality, and deployment measurements.

lessons.title: Root trust anchors and key rollover
learning_goals: Explain RFC 5011 hold-down, overlap, and revocation.
Distinguish a valid local update protocol from evidence of global readiness.
source_sections: 9. Root trust anchors and key rollover

lessons.title: Encrypted DNS and resolver trust
learning_goals: Compare DoT, DoH, and DoQ with DNSSEC.
Identify what on-path observers and the receiving resolver can still learn.

lessons.title: QNAME minimisation and Oblivious DoH
learning_goals: Explain how minimisation reduces disclosures to authoritative servers.
Trace which information an Oblivious DoH relay and target receive.

lessons.title: Anycast DNS and routing-based recovery
learning_goals: Distinguish root identities from their physical instances.
Explain route-selected replicas and the detection and convergence needed after failure.

lessons.title: Stale delegation, expired signatures, and poisoned caches
learning_goals: Distinguish three persistent DNS failure modes.
Separate local detection from the authority or information needed for repair.

lessons.title: DNS investigation and revision
learning_goals: Use nslookup and dig to distinguish answers, referrals, and validation evidence.
Apply the lecture revision checklist across naming, caching, trust, and privacy.

question_links.rationale: The alias lesson teaches target following and supplies a combined CNAME/address response example; its clarification explains the key's overstatement.
question_links.review_note: A CNAME requires following a target name, but not necessarily another network query: the target address may be in the same answer or cache. The keyed option overstates the extra lookup.
question_links.next_action: Review the gap or wording before scored practice; do not change the original key automatically.

question_links.rationale: The resolution walk shows a root referral to TLD servers.

question_links.rationale: The negative-caching explanation gives the lesser-of-two-TTL rule, which is more precise than the keyed option.
question_links.review_note: NXDOMAIN denotes nonexistence. Its negative-cache lifetime is limited by the lesser of SOA.MINIMUM and the SOA RR TTL, not SOA.MINIMUM alone; the keyed option omits that condition.
question_links.next_action: Review the gap or wording before scored practice; do not change the original key automatically.
